description.text:
Wizards of the Coast started the Pokémon League in the United States in June 1999, after prototype leagues that spring, and ran it in toy, book and game shops. Members earned points for turning up, playing, trading and teaching the game, stamped into a badge book, and each season had a promo card: one copy at 250 points and a second at 500. Ivy Pikachu, Wizards Black Star Promo 1, was the first, from July 1999, and from January 2000 everyone who joined a League got a non-holo Mew. Wizards also made Trainer Decks A and B for the first Leagues, decks it never sold.

The second year, from January 2001, followed the eight Johto Gym badges: a gold and silver badge book had a page for each, and each badge had its own promo, starting with Togepi for the Zephyr Badge at 400 points. The third year, Energize Your Game, ran from 6 January to October 2002 in eight seasons. Players filled a license with stamps, two for a win and one for a loss, earning an older "classic" promo first and then a new one, and those who played a season's closing tournament earned its foil Energy. BattleZone, Wizards' last League, from November 2002, gave out the Best of Game cards: copies stamped Winner for top players and a jumbo Winner copy in each season's prize kit; two of them came out unstamped later, as classic promos. Wizards lost the Pokémon license before the June and July 2003 seasons were played, but their prize kits had already gone out, so those two cards exist only as Winner copies.

Pokémon Organized Play ran the League from September 2003. That month's kit, meant for 16 players, held 16 reverse-holo Torchic, 8 Combusken stamped Winner and one jumbo Combusken for a winner of the store's choosing, and kits held a jumbo every month until March 2004 except December. The seasons of that 2003-2004 Hoenn cycle also gave cosmos holo cards with Winner-stamped twins (Bulbapedia's set lists call it the e-League), and from June to August 2004 the kits held plain and Winner copies of Beldum, Chimecho and Flygon.

Later Leagues handed out holofoil copies of expansion cards, each named for the season that gave it: crosshatch holo with the Pokémon League logo from September 2009, with the Play! Pokémon logo instead from September 2011 to July 2012, and with the League logo again from 2013 to 2015, then mirror holo from November 2015 and reverse holo from February 2016 to 2020. The Evolutions seasons of 2016-2017 gave a holo Pikachu and eight Gym Badges. In early 2023 Leagues received the staff copies of the Evolving Skies, Brilliant Stars, Astral Radiance and Lost Origin prerelease promos, and reverse holo League copies came back in June and July 2024 and again in 2025.
